title: Apples vs Apples: Load Synthesis & KV/Batching Calibration — Pegasus Industries
summary: Technical workshop to align on an apples-to-apples benchmarking protocol for Pegasus' on-prem inference pilot. Covered prompt sets, load synthesis (replay vs synthetic), KV cache priming, batching strategies, quantization profiles, and VPC/on-prem constraints. Agreed to run two controlled runs (baseline FP16 hosted vs quantized on-prem) and a replayed user load for 72 hours. Action items assigned for artifact handoff and test infra automation.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 1:30
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Pegasus CTO), Sofia Alvarez (Lead ML), Marcus Cho (Infra), Priya Nair (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete)
- Goal: agree benchmark protocol to compare hosted vs on-prem quantized runs
- Key constraints: Pegasus requires VPC-only egress, KMS integration, and audit logs retained 1 year

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here.
[00:07] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia on my side.
[00:09] Marcus Cho: Marcus.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Priya.
[00:12] Jordan Li: Jordan, se from Redwood.
[00:14] Ava Martinez: Cool, goal today is to produce an apples-to-apples protocol we can both run. We'll talk prompts, load, caching, quant, and the on-prem constraints.

[00:35] Sofia Alvarez: Quick context — our production is mixture of short chat prompts and longer document summarization. Roughly 70% short, 30% long with median tokens 64 but 95th at around 1,200.
[00:48] Marcus Cho: And we care a lot about p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts, but also tail behaviour for longer sequences.

[01:12] Jordan Li: Important to capture sequence distribution in the load generator. If we syntheticize everything you'll miss cache hit patterns. We recommend a replay where possible, and a synthetic overlay to stress corner cases.

[01:40] Sofia Alvarez: We can share sanitized replay logs — need to know which fields to strip.
[01:46] Ava Martinez: Great, we'll send a script. Ideally timestamped requests + tokens, model variant, and whether the user requested streaming. Strip PII before handoff.

[02:08] Priya Nair: On prem note — we run in an internal VPC, outbound egress is blocked except via our proxy. Networking and audit logs are required for compliance.
[02:20] Ava Martinez: Redwood Privet — sorry, Redwood Private — supports VPC mode with customer-managed egress. We'll note the proxy requirement.

[02:45] Rajiv Menon: For apples-to-apples, we want to compare: hosted FP16 baseline, dedicated reserved Redwood, and on-prem quantized (8-bit or 4-bit). Also want to see cost per 1M tokens basis.

[03:10] Jordan Li: Agreed. We'll define a baseline model and a quantization profile. For quant, we suggest testing two profiles: 8-bit symmetric and a more aggressive 4-bit with per-channel calibration. We'll capture quality via our eval harness using BLEU/ROUGE and some domain-specific scoring.

[03:48] Sofia Alvarez: How do you recommend priming KV cache for the replay? Our traffic has a lot of short multi-turn sessions.
[03:55] Jordan Li: Two-step approach: 1) Session-aligned replay to preserve KV cache continuity for multi-turn, 2) Synthetic warm-up that replays most common prefixes to reach steady-state hit rates. We'll measure cache hit ratio over time.

[04:30] Marcus Cho: What's the impact of batching on latency? We saw previous tests where increasing batch size dropped throughput variance but spiked p99.
[04:38] Jordan Li: Right. Continuous batching improves throughput but can add extra queuing latency. We recommend measuring latency SLOs under two queueing policies: immediate dispatch (low-latency) and controlled batching with max batch time 15ms and max batch size tuned by throughput target. We'll include both in the protocol.

[05:10] Ava Martinez: We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token-level breakdowns in the console export. Also include cold-start vs warmed runtime numbers.

[05:40] Sofia Alvarez: For quality checks after quant, what's the acceptance criteria? Our product team won't accept more than a 1.5% delta in key extraction F1 score.
[05:49] Jordan Li: We'll set thresholds per metric. In our protocol we'll include paired-rank tests (statistical) and per-prompt thresholds. If an aggressive quant profile exceeds delta, we fall back to 8-bit.

[06:12] Rajiv Menon: Also want to validate KV cache memory footprint on our nodes — how to measure?
[06:18] Jordan Li: We'll instrument KV cache metrics: total entries, bytes, and eviction rates. The starter script will sample metrics and attach them to benchmark artifacts. Marcus, we'll need prometheus endpoints or a metrics push to your internal metric sink.

[06:55] Marcus Cho: We can expose a metrics endpoint on the bastion. Concern: logs and artifacts cannot leave our VPC.
[07:02] Ava Martinez: We can run everything in the VPC and have the Redwood agent upload artifacts to an S3-like bucket inside their network. Or use an on-prem console instance. We'll send options in the protocol doc.

[07:34] Sofia Alvarez: On load generation fidelity: replay vs replay+jitter. We want to ensure inter-arrival variability is captured.
[07:41] Jordan Li: Add jitter sampled from your observed distribution — don't use pure Poisson unless that's what you saw. We'll provide a replay loader that preserves original timestamps and offers a jitter parameter.

[08:05] Priya Nair: Security — we need audit logs per-request, and SSO integration for the trial accounts. Also KMS for key wrapping of model weights.
[08:13] Ava Martinez: Redwood Private supports KMS and HSM integrations; we'll include our SOC2/ISO docs. Jordan, can you attach the security pack?
[08:20] Jordan Li: I'll upload the security pack to the secure link (see note).

[08:45] Rajiv Menon: On metrics, please include breakdown: scheduling time, kernel time, quant overhead, memory GC events.
[08:53] Jordan Li: We'll add those counters. Our runtime emits kernel-level timing and queuing times; quant overhead is measured during model load and token step.

[09:20] Sofia Alvarez: We need a reproducible seed for sampling and the same model weights across runs. How do we pin weights?
[09:27] Jordan Li: We'll include a model digest (sha256) and an artifact registry reference. For hosted baseline we'll provide the model digest; for on-prem you'll pin to the same digest or to a Redwood-verified quantized artifact.

[09:55] Marcus Cho: Network variability is a big unknown with our users. Should we add a network emulation step?
[10:01] Ava Martinez: Yes — include two network profiles: 1) low-latency LAN (no emulation), 2) degraded network (100ms added RTT and 1% loss) to see tail effects. We'll add both to the protocol.

[10:30] Sofia Alvarez: Regarding the eval harness, can we run it locally so data doesn't leave our VPC?
[10:36] Jordan Li: Absolutely, the harness can run in your VPC. It produces a zipped artifact for internal review. If you want Redwood to analyze, you can share via secure transfer.

[11:05] Rajiv Menon: What does an apples-to-apples cost comparison look like? I want $/M tokens plus infra ops overhead and amortized quantization engineering time.
[11:14] Ava Martinez: We'll provide a cost model template: runtime cost per token (power + cloud + reserved commit amortization), ops time baseline, and quant engineering effort bucketed as one-time cost. We'll populate with Redwood sample numbers and you can slot in your infra rates.

[11:40] Priya Nair: Compliance asks for 12 months of audit logs and a retention TTL. Can Redwood support that?
[11:46] Ava Martinez: Yes, we can configure retention policy for audit logs on Redwood Private and export to your SIEM. We'll include config steps in the doc.

[12:10] Sofia Alvarez: Let's quickly sketch the experimental matrix so we don't leave ambiguity.
[12:15] Jordan Li: Proposal: 3x model states (hosted FP16 baseline, on-prem 8-bit quant, on-prem 4-bit quant), 2x batching policies (low-latency immediate, controlled batch with 15ms max delay), 2x load types (replay, synthetic stress), 2x network profiles. That's 24 cells; run each cell for 2 hours and one 72-hour replay run for end-to-end stability.

[12:55] Rajiv Menon: 24 cells is heavy but seems reasonable. Suggest we prioritize the cells that map to short prompts first.

[13:10] Marcus Cho: For the 72h run, we'll need automation to rotate logs and avoid disk fill.
[13:16] Jordan Li: We'll include log rotation in the starter scripts.

[13:40] Ava Martinez: Ok quick note on evaluation: we'll publish a canonical prompt set of 250 prompts covering short, mid, and long. We'll also include 50 adversarial prompts targeted at hallucination checks.

[14:05] Sofia Alvarez: How do we handle failure cases where quant causes catastrophic flips?
[14:11] Jordan Li: We'll have a rollback policy and an automatic quality gate: if delta>threshold for more than N samples, terminate run and fall back to previous profile.

[14:40] Priya Nair: Any objections or gaps we missed?
[14:45] Rajiv Menon: Need data residency verification for model artifacts and encryption in transit.
[14:52] Ava Martinez: We'll document the residency guarantees, and Jordan will attach encryption in transit docs.

[15:10] Jordan Li: I'll also provide the starter loadgen with a parameterized KV priming tool. Expect that in the shared folder.

[15:35] Sofia Alvarez: We'll prep sanitized logs and narrow down the short-prompt priority set.

[15:50] Ava Martinez: Great. Final recap: Redwood sends protocol + prompt set + security pack; Pegasus shares logs and opens Bastion; SEs provision test node and run initial prioritized runs next week.

[16:05] Rajiv Menon: That works. Thanks, team.
[16:10] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-corrected (Redwood Private as Privet), KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash', quantization as 'quand-tization'. There are occasional overlapping speakers and truncated timestamps.

- Prompt set (canonical): https://redwood.example.com/artifacts/pegasus-promptset-250.zip
- Starter scripts and loadgen: https://redwood.example.com/repos/bench-starter/pegasus

End of transcript.
